dialect.detail: IBM mainframe IMS/DLI batch subprogram; uses PCB (Program Communication Block) structure typical of IMS DL/I, SET ADDRESS OF, GOBACK, and sequence numbers in linkage section
evidence: PCB-AREA with DBD-NAME, SEG-LEVEL, ST-CODE, PROC-OPT, KEFEDBAK
SET ADDRESS OF PCB-AREA TO LNKDB-PTRPCB
sequence numbers on linkage section lines (00000700 etc.)
ISRT, DLET and REPL commands reference

purpose.domain_detail: IMS/DLI database access middleware; batch routine template for DL/I ISRT, DLET and REPL operations
purpose.summary: This is a batch subprogram (routine) that serves as a template/skeleton for IMS DL/I database operations (ISRT, DLET, REPL). It initializes working areas, sets up PCB addressing, handles error routing with action codes, and returns to the caller. The actual command recognition logic is marked as a placeholder (#OPE#) to be filled in.

notable_features: IMS DL/I PCB structure in LINKAGE SECTION
SET ADDRESS OF for PCB pointer
COPY ERRVSMRT and COPY LNKDBRT copybooks
Large working storage areas (5x 12000-byte data areas + 400-byte SSA areas)
Error routing section with action codes (ACTION-NOOP, ACTION-DLSA)
Placeholder markers #CODE# and #OPE# suggesting template/generated skeleton
Sequence numbers on linkage section lines
verdict.notes: The program appears to be a skeleton/template with placeholder markers (#OPE#, #CODE#) indicating that the actual DL/I command dispatch logic has been removed or is to be inserted. The CALL 'NOOP' and immediate GO TO 3000-MAIN-END confirm this is a stub. Italian-language field names (DATA-CREAZ, ACTION-ERRORE, CODDB-NOER) suggest Italian development team. Last modification date 06 04 2005, Release 2.1.
